summary: PubConnect Phase 2.0 customer backend tested end-to-end at /app/backend/tests/test_phase2_customer.py (31 tests, 100% pass). Verified: customer registration (email, mobile, both), duplicate email/mobile -> generic 409, login via email AND mobile for seeded demo user, generic 401 'Invalid credentials' for both unknown-user and wrong-password (no account enumeration), no password_hash in any response. Verified JWT aud separation: customer token accepted on all 6 customer endpoints and REJECTED (401) on 6 admin endpoints; admin token REJECTED (401) on customer endpoints. IDOR: created customers A and B, confirmed /auth/me returns only self, cross-customer GET /transactions/{id} returns 404 (not 403), transactions list contains only own entries. PAY QR tokens are opaque, carry no PII in response or token value, ttl=5min, single-use (second resolve -> 400 'already been used'), unknown token -> 404 (proves pub-scoping). Admin-generated REDEEM token still resolves. Profile PATCH updates and 409 on duplicate email in pub. Notification preferences GET + partial PATCH persist. Login rate limit returns 429 after ~10/min. Phase 1 regression smoke (dashboard, customers list, offers list, transactions, audit, BAR_STAFF 403 on /staff and POST /offers) all pass.

minor.issue: Unique index on (pub_id, mobile_number) has NO partialFilterExpression (unlike the email index). A second email-only registration (mobile_number omitted/null) hits a duplicate-key error on {mobile_number: null} and the server returns a generic 409 'Unable to register with the provided details'. In practice email-only signups beyond the first in a given pub always fail. Fix: add partialFilterExpression={'mobile_number': {'$type': 'string'}} to the mobile index (mirror of the email one in server.py startup()).

action_items: Fix mobile_number unique index to use partialFilterExpression {'mobile_number': {'$type': 'string'}} so email-only registrations don't collide on null (server.py startup()).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~1360 lines; split into resource modules (admin_auth, customer_auth, ledger, offers, action_tokens, staff).

jwt.decode uses options={'verify_aud': False} and aud is checked manually — works but surprising; set an issuer or validate audience natively per guard (pass audience='admin'/'customer') to catch mistakes.
Rate limit is in-memory per process; behind multiple workers/replicas limits become per-replica and effectively weaker. Fine for MVP, flag for production.
Customer registration catches ALL exceptions as 409 (`except Exception`), masking any true 500 — narrow to pymongo DuplicateKeyError.
Index design bug noted in backend_issues.minor is the direct cause of hidden 409s.
_single_pub() silently falls back to any pub when ADMIN_EMAIL owner missing — ok for seed, but log/warn in production.

rca of the issue: RCA for the email-only registration 409: FastAPI startup() creates `db.customers.create_index([('pub_id', 1), ('mobile_number', 1)], unique=True)` WITHOUT a partialFilterExpression. The companion email index DOES have `partialFilterExpression={'email': {'$type': 'string'}}`. So when a customer registers with email only, their stored document has mobile_number=null (or missing). A second such registration triggers a duplicate-key error on {pub_id, mobile_number: null}. The register handler's try/except catches it generically and converts to HTTP 409 'Unable to register with the provided details'. Reproduction: POST /api/customer/auth/register with distinct emails and no mobile_number -> first succeeds, every subsequent one 409s. Mitigation (one-line): mirror the email index with partialFilterExpression={'mobile_number': {'$type': 'string'}} so nulls are excluded from the unique constraint. Existing documents with mobile_number=null need to be re-indexed (drop+recreate on startup is already how indexes are managed; MongoDB will rebuild).
